negative_findings.description: No official Slovak PSD3/PSR transposition tracker, draft bill, or announced national deadline was found in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: SK-language searches on PSD3 transposition returned only law-firm commentary and an NBS explanatory PDF; no MF SR draft act, no Slov-Lex legislative process item, no NBS PSD3 hub. Consistent with PSD3/PSR not yet being in force, but means the SK transposition clock cannot be documented from a primary source today.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PSD3/PSR is the largest pending payments obligation for SK banks and PSPs; the absence of a SK primary tracker means the run must rely on EU-level milestones until MF SR opens a comment procedure.

negative_findings.description: No published SBA (Slovenská banková asociácia) position paper on PSD3/PSR was located.
negative_findings.result_summary: SBA site returned general news items and one piece on an EU payment-security directive, but no PSD3 stanovisko. SBA's news archive may hold one behind non-indexed pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Industry positions are the main indirect read on how SK banks expect to be affected; absence leaves a gap in sector-side signal for payments regulation.

negative_findings.description: No SK-specific ECB/SSM supervisory decision register was found — ECB does not publish individual supervisory decisions per bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only the aggregate list of supervised entities and general SSM materials. Slovakia currently has no domestically headquartered significant institution; nine SK LSIs are listed, two high-impact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank-level ECB decisions on SK entities are structurally non-public; the run must substitute the supervised-entities list, SREP aggregates and NBS LSI supervision outputs.

negative_findings.description: No stable Slovak-language term set exists for PSR (Payment Services Regulation) and AMLA.
negative_findings.result_summary: SK sources use the English acronyms PSD3/PSR/AMLA verbatim, or long descriptive phrases ('nariadenie o platobných službách'); no consolidated SK glossary was found beyond the NBS payments-law PDF.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring queries will under-recall unless English-in-Slovak acronyms are searched alongside descriptive SK phrases.

coverage_gaps.description: AMLA (the new EU AML Authority, Frankfurt) was not reached as a source in this pass; its selection of directly supervised entities and its SK-facing guidance are not yet covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add AMLA's official site and its first selection/guidance publications to the source set, and pair with the SK Financial Intelligence Unit (FSJ, Prezídium Policajného zboru MV SR) as the national counterpart.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level consultation calendars (Commission 'Have your say', EBA public consultations, ESAs joint consultations) were not individually catalogued, so forward-looking deadline signals are under-covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ec.europa.eu/info/law/better-regulation/have-your-say, EBA consultation-paper listing, and the ESAs joint committee page, filtered to banking/payments, with SK stakeholder responses flagged.

coverage_gaps.description: The SK pre-legislative comment procedure (medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie) on Slov-Lex was identified but not exercised — no confirmed query pattern for locating MF SR financial-market transposition bills.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish a Slov-Lex open-data/API query for LP items submitted by MF SR with a transposition annex referencing EU financial-services acts; this is the earliest possible SK deadline signal.

coverage_gaps.description: CRR3/CRD6 (banking package) SK application and the EU MiCA/crypto and Basel output-floor deadlines were not searched in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on CRR3/CRD6 and MiCA SK transposition/authorisation deadlines via NBS legislatíva, MF SR and EUR-Lex NIM.

coverage_gaps.description: Two key registers (EBA EUCLID payment institutions register, Slov-Lex search) are client-side applications whose collectability was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe for JSON/API endpoints or bulk downloads for both before designing collectors; do not assume HTML scraping works.

brief: The EU-to-Slovakia regulatory pipeline is well documented at the EU end and thinly documented at the Slovak end. EUR-Lex's national transposition register, the Single Market Scoreboard, EBA compliance tables and the ECB's CON opinions on Slovak draft laws give authoritative, datable coverage of what lands on SK and when, while NBS mirrors this nationally through per-guideline compliance declarations and topic hubs for DORA, instant payments/Verification of Payee, and the AML package. The weakest link is forward-looking: PSD3/PSR has no Slovak primary tracker yet, ECB bank-level supervisory decisions on SK entities are structurally non-public, and the earliest SK signal — the MF SR draft bill entering the medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie on Slov-Lex — needs a working query pattern before it can be monitored. Slovak-language sourcing was productive for regulator hubs and law-firm bulletins, but SK practice imports the English acronyms PSD3, PSR, DORA and AMLA verbatim, so bilingual query design is mandatory rather than optional.
